title: Rectangular object
spec: Create a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector set to zero, zero, and zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the plane defined by this coordinate system. In this first sketch, draw the first face using a single loop. Start by drawing the first line from the origin at zero, zero to zero point zero two nine three, zero. Then, draw the second line from zero point zero two nine three, zero to zero point zero two nine three, zero point zero zero five nine. Continue by drawing the third line from zero point zero two nine three, zero point zero zero five nine to zero, zero point zero zero five nine. Finally, draw the fourth line from zero, zero point zero zero five nine back to the origin at zero, zero. Apply a scaling factor of zero point zero two nine three to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it using the same translation vector. Extrude the transformed two-dimensional sketch along the normal direction by zero point seven five units to create a new solid body. Ensure that no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction of the normal. The final dimensions of the rectangular object are length zero point zero two nine three units, width zero point zero zero five nine units, and height zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.box(0.0293, 0.0059, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False))

# The box command creates a box with the specified dimensions
# The centered parameter is set to False to ensure the box starts from the origin (0, 0, 0)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · best of 8
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0293) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0293) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0059)

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Thin flat bar with rounded corners: 0.75 x 0.0293 x 0.0059
w = 0.75
h = 0.0293
t = 0.0059
r_c = h / 2  # fully rounded (semicircular) ends as seen in the RIGHT view

# Sketch the top profile with rounded ends
r = cq.Workplane("XY") \
    .moveTo(r_c, 0) \
    .lineTo(w - r_c, 0) \
    .threePointArc((w, h / 2), (w - r_c, h)) \
    .lineTo(r_c, h) \
    .threePointArc((0, h / 2), (r_c, 0)) \
    .close() \
    .extrude(t)
